requirements.title: Character selectors preserve each length and kind keyword ordering
requirements.definition: A char-selector can be a length-selector; (LEN=L,KIND=K); (L,K); (L,KIND=K); (KIND=K); or (KIND=K,LEN=L). Here L is a type-param-value subject to its enclosing context, and K is a scalar integer constant expression satisfying C724. The length-first keyword form requires KIND=, while the kind-first form requires LEN= if a length is supplied. A single positional expression specifies length, not kind. The expression specifying KIND need not itself have default integer kind, but any conversion used to produce its value must be representable.

pending.length-selector-alternative: Planned finite link to the future R722_valid__parentheses and R722_valid__star_forms controls. Review both descendant alternatives rather than adding a duplicate wrapper execution. Omitted CHARACTER selectors remain owned by R704 and S7.4.4.2-001/004.
pending.integer-expression-kind: Planned qualified run R721_valid__selected_expression_kind. First establish KIND('A') < 10**10 by ten default-integer divisions in a separate character-kind-code-decimal10 profile, without evaluating that power in default integer. Then store the identifier in an integer PARAMETER whose kind is SELECTED_INT_KIND(18), and use it in the character selector. The independent decimal bound makes the conversion representable in the F2023-required range-18 method; no 1/4/8 identifier or greater-than-default range is assumed. Check the declared character kind and value. A larger identifier makes only this finite witness unavailable; missing mandatory range-18 support remains a failure. The selected expression kind may equal default.
pending.kind-expression-premises: Planned canonical compile pairs C401_invalid__character_kind_array/C401_valid__character_kind_scalar, C1009_invalid__character_kind_real/C1009_valid__character_kind_integer, and C1014_invalid__character_kind_variable/C1014_valid__character_kind_parameter. Repair [KIND('A')] to KIND('A'), real 1.0 to KIND('A'), and an initialized integer variable to a PARAMETER respectively. Require scalar-rank, integer-type and genuine constancy causes separately. Add a bounded source-use graph for R403/C401, R1027/C1009 and R1032/C1014; keep those defining owners. The separate expression-kind witness has its own independent identifier-conversion bound, not a presumption that a selected integer method can hold every default-integer identifier.

requirements.oracle: Five run controls cover the kind-bearing selector orderings, with exact LEN, KIND and value assertions. Two one-substitution compile pairs isolate the LEN-first and KIND-first keyword exclusions. Their predicates require the specific offending token or ordering cause, not generic expected-parenthesis recovery. Canonical expression-category and optional bounded identifier-conversion work remains pending. Direct case IDs: R721_invalid__kind_keyword_positional_length, R721_invalid__len_keyword_positional_kind, R721_valid__kind_keyword_positional_length_repair, R721_valid__kind_len_keywords, R721_valid__kind_only, R721_valid__len_keyword_positional_kind_repair, R721_valid__len_kind_keywords, R721_valid__positional, R721_valid__positional_keyword.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Direct cases are authored but not independently approved. Scalar LEN does not imply constant LEN in all scopes; scalar constant KIND is different from LEN's context-specific specification expression. Reporting follows numbered syntax/constraints and 4.2 p2(3), not compulsory fatal rejection. Use exact source relations and case-specific causal predicates; crashes, ASR verifier errors, unsupported language features and wrong-source recovery cannot pass.

The corrected diagnostic/identifier principles are recorded in doc/source_audits/batch_009.json.

requirements.title: Length selectors have parenthesized and star forms
requirements.definition: A length-selector is a parenthesized type-param-value with optional LEN=, or a star followed by char-length and an optional comma. The latter comma is only permitted under C729 and C730. R701 supplies the scalar integer expression, assumed asterisk and deferred colon alternatives; C704, C702, C726, C731 and other enclosing rules determine which uses are legal. Neither OPTIONAL nor ALLOCATABLE/POINTER alone bans an assumed-length character dummy.

pending.length-expression-premises: Planned canonical compile pairs C401_invalid__character_len_array/C401_valid__character_len_scalar and C1009_invalid__character_len_real/C1009_valid__character_len_integer, repairing [3] to 3 and 3.0 to 3. For restricted-expression context, review existing C704_invalid__optional_length and add companion C704_valid__character_optional_repair by removing only OPTIONAL from its integer n declaration. The invalid condition is using optional n in LEN=n, not declaring an optional CHARACTER(*) dummy. Preserve C702's existing missing-attribute/repair pair and record a finite C704/C805/C759 use graph for ordinary, individual and component lengths. Each negative needs its own scalar/type/restricted-expression cause at the actual length expression; no broad constant/expected matcher.

requirements.oracle: Run controls exercise both parenthesized forms, both legacy star forms, the optional legacy comma without ::, and small integer-kind-selected length expressions. The SELECTED_INT_KIND(4) witness uses only value 3; default integer range at least five guarantees a qualifying method, not a distinct or wider kind. Direct case IDs: R722_valid__comma, R722_valid__parentheses, R722_valid__selected_length_expression, R722_valid__star_forms.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The optional comma is not generally allowed in ALLOCATE, components, TYPE wrappers or function prefixes. The older CHARACTER* form is obsolescent, not deleted. The four deferred establishment mechanisms are already planned/covered under the 7.2 owner; this syntax wrapper does not relabel those effects.
requirements.dependencies: R701/C702 (PDF 76), C704/C707 (PDF 77), R723/C726/C729-C731 (PDF 84-85), C759 (PDF 93), C805 (PDF 118), 10.1.11 p1-p2/C1011 (PDF 185-187), and 8.5.12/C851 (PDF 130). 7.4.3.1 p4 and 16.9.181 (PDF 80, 454-455) justify the small selected-integer length expression. B.3.8 (PDF 579) retains the older form's obsolescent status; 4.2 p2(2)-(3) (PDF 46) distinguishes obsolescence reporting from a syntax violation.

requirements.title: Individual star lengths admit a parenthesized value or bare integer literal
requirements.definition: A char-length is a parenthesized type-param-value or an int-literal-constant. Parenthesized expressions can include signs and operations; the bare alternative is not a signed expression or a name. Parenthesized asterisks and colons retain C726 and C702 placement requirements. C725 restricts the bare integer-literal alternative, not every integer literal nested inside a parenthesized expression.
requirements.oracle: Run controls use bare integers, parenthesized arithmetic/negative/zero values and individual assumed/deferred lengths in legal dummy/ALLOCATABLE/POINTER contexts. Allocation/association is established before deferred inquiries. A compile pair repairs an unparenthesized sum by adding its parentheses. Direct case IDs: R723_invalid__bare_expression, R723_valid__assumed_deferred, R723_valid__bare_expression_repair, R723_valid__expression, R723_valid__integer.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No byte-size meaning is assigned to star lengths, and no negative-expression rejection is inferred. The assumed/deferred controls are context-qualified syntax admission with runtime checks, not a full proof of all argument/allocation semantics.

requirements.title: A character selector kind is nonnegative and supported
requirements.definition: The scalar integer constant expression selecting character kind has a nonnegative value and identifies a character representation method supported by the processor. This is independent of whether the expression is scalar, integer and constant. Zero is not universally an invalid kind, and a kind supported for another intrinsic type need not be a supported character kind.

pending.unsupported-nonnegative-kind: Planned compile diagnose C724_invalid__absent_zero and control C724_valid__absent_zero_repair after an independent character-kind-zero-absent profile establishes that 0 is absent from CHARACTER_KINDS. Repair only 0 to KIND('A'). A processor supporting zero makes this finite witness unavailable, not passed. The profile must not compile the invalid declaration, and a failed inventory query is not an absence result.

requirements.oracle: Unprofiled compile controls use a supported KIND inquiry. A negative/control pair changes only -1 to KIND('A'). Unsupported representation-value reports are intended; false constancy and unsupported-language-feature reports are excluded. Nonnegative absent-kind witnesses remain pending independent qualification. Direct case IDs: C724_invalid__negative, C724_valid__negative_repair, C724_valid__supported.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Numbered reporting capability and 4.2 p2(4) do not require fatal rejection in every mode or particular words. Case-specific source/value predicates must exclude generic kind/parameter strings, wrong constancy causes, crashes, verifier failures, resource errors and wrong-source recovery. No full supported-kind inventory is proved by these three cases.
requirements.dependencies: R721; 7.4.4.1 p2 and 7.4.4.2 p2-p3 (PDF 84); 16.9.118 (PDF 424); 16.10.2.4 (PDF 472); 4.2 p2(3)-(4) (PDF 46). doc/source_audits/batch_009.json provides the corrected causal-report pattern, not a compiler-consensus oracle.

requirements.title: A bare star-length integer literal has no kind suffix
requirements.definition: The int-literal-constant occurring as R723's bare alternative has no kind-param. This does not ban kind-suffixed integer literals inside the scalar integer expression of the parenthesized type-param-value alternative.
requirements.oracle: The compile pair deletes only the kind suffix from a bare star length. The independent run retains that supported integer suffix inside parenthesized length expressions and checks length/value. No global ban on kind-suffixed length expressions is introduced. Direct case IDs: C725_invalid__bare_suffix, C725_valid__bare_suffix_repair, C725_valid__parenthesized_suffix.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Do not reject all nondefault integer length expressions or assume ik is a byte count. No conversion of a character-kind identifier to another integer method is involved.

requirements.title: Assumed character length has an explicit context whitelist
requirements.source: 7.4.4.2 C726 (R721 R722 R723); PDF 84, printed 70, lines 39-43, continuing PDF 85, printed 71, lines 1-2.
requirements.definition:
An asterisk length value is admitted for a dummy argument, a named constant, an ALLOCATE type-spec when every allocate-object is a CHARACTER dummy with assumed character length, a type guard's type-spec or derived-type-spec, or the declaration of an external function result within that external function. The list is not limited to ordinary nonoptional, nonallocatable, nonpointer dummies. Other constraints still apply, including actual/dummy parameter agreement, C727-C728 for functions, C939 for allocation, C1165 for type guards, and C7100 for derived-type parameter uses.

An ordinary local variable, a character component, an internal/module function result, a nondummy allocate-object or a deferred rather than assumed dummy does not gain assumed length merely because another example is allowed. In a multi-object ALLOCATE every object must meet the condition. The introductory explanation in 7.2 p7 is not a global ban on the explicit external-function and ALLOCATE exceptions here.

pending.optional-dummies: Planned admission link to the separate run effect S7_4_4_2_006_valid__optional. OPTIONAL is legal here; absent paths must not inquire LEN or reference the missing argument. The canonical-link proposal remains pending until parent integration.
pending.allocatable-and-pointer-dummies: Planned admission links to S7_4_4_2_006_valid__allocatable_dummy and S7_4_4_2_006_valid__pointer_dummy. Use nondeferred character lengths on both actuals and assumed-length dummies, matching allocation/pointer attributes and explicit interfaces. Neither attribute itself forbids the star.
pending.allocate-assumed-dummies: Planned admission link to S7_4_4_2_006_valid__allocate_assumed for allocatable and pointer dummy variants, with all allocate-objects assumed length. Read C939's if-and-only-if condition and check each actual's nondeferred length; do not substitute a local deferred object as the positive control.
pending.derived-type-guard-connection: Record the finite derived-type guard connection to R754/C7100/C1165 and existing S7_2_005_valid__select_type_pdt after parent review. Do not assign PDT defining ownership to this character catalogue or treat a CLASS IS intrinsic-character guard as valid. C726_valid's PDT dummy is not a derived-type guard execution.
pending.external-result: Planned admission link to S7_4_4_2_006_valid__external, an actual separate external assumed-length function with legal explicit caller lengths. The existing C726_valid does not exercise this allowance and must not be described as doing so.

requirements.oracle: The six retained negative executions now have separate adjacent-sidecar facets, source/cause contracts and review keys. Their original container bytes and IDs are unchanged. Each has a one-star repaired compile control. Module/internal results use only the two-line function/result-declaration relation; the unrelated enclosing PRINT is excluded. The retained positive preserves its runtime body and covers only ordinary character dummies, a named constant and a CHARACTER guard. Its misleading comment is corrected. A separate mixed-allocation pair removes only the unqualified local object from the all-assumed-dummy list. Optional/PDT guard and other allowance linkage remains pending; actual missing allocation/external effects are authored under S7.4.4.2-006. Direct case IDs: C726_invalid:allocate-dummy-deferred, C726_invalid:allocate-local, C726_invalid:component, C726_invalid:internal-function-result, C726_invalid:local-variable, C726_invalid:module-function-result, C726_invalid__allocate_mixed, C726_valid, C726_valid__allocate_deferred_repair, C726_valid__allocate_local_repair, C726_valid__allocate_mixed_repair, C726_valid__component_repair, C726_valid__internal_result_repair, C726_valid__local_repair, C726_valid__module_result_repair.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No old approval is reused. The original negative container and positive runtime body are preserved; the positive metadata does not cover OPTIONAL, ALLOCATE, external results or a derived-type guard. The ordinary/optional and character/derived-guard facets are refined transparently for B010-L02. Each negative has one genuine facet and a minimal control, never the container-wide union. Case-specific reporting excludes feature failures, crashes, ASR verifier errors, generic expected/function/type strings, obsolescence and wrong-source recovery. The remaining allowance/link facets remain pending until parent integration.
requirements.dependencies: R701/C702 and 7.2 p7 (PDF 76); C727-C728 and p5 (PDF 85); C759 (PDF 93); R754/C7100 (PDF 106); C939 and 9.7.1.1 p6 (PDF 160, 162); R1156/C1165 and 11.1.11.2 p5-p7 (PDF 225-226); 15.5.2.5 p5, 15.5.2.6 p3-p4, 15.5.2.7-.8 and 15.5.2.13 (PDF 340, 343, 346); 15.6.2.1 p3/C1564 and 15.6.2.2 (PDF 353-354). In particular C1564 restricts BIND(C) dummy lengths, not ordinary Fortran dummies; no BIND(C) fixture is inferred here.

requirements.title: Only character dummy functions and external result names admit star length
requirements.definition: C727 conditions a function name declared with an asterisk type-param-value on CHARACTER type and on being a dummy-function name or an external-function result name. The application of the external-name/result-name distinction to an unused CHARACTER(*),EXTERNAL declaration in a nondefining scope remains unresolved here; this catalogue does not assert that declaration is forbidden. The separate p5 declaration/access obligation applies to scopes that invoke or pass the function, so it does not apply to this unused declaration. A fixed-length external declaration is a bounded admission control outside the asterisk condition, not evidence that the corresponding unused star declaration is invalid.

pending.character-premise: Planned finite source-use graph character-function-star-type: connect R704's six alternatives, R706, R721-R723 and C701 with this CHARACTER-only premise. Do not fabricate an INTEGER(*) function as an isolated C727 negative; its kind-selector grammar/constancy is already defective. No documentary evidence case type currently represents this graph.
pending.external-result-declaration: Planned finite link to the external definition in S7_4_4_2_006_valid__external. Keep the result declaration within that external subprogram and satisfy every C728 exclusion; internal/module result exclusions retain the existing C726 identities.
pending.caller-declaration-exclusion: Pending interpretation after CTP2-002; the historical facet identity is retained, not a settled exclusion claim. Establish the exact application of C726/C727 external-name/result-name wording to an unused CHARACTER(*),EXTERNAL declaration before proposing any new negative. The p5 invocation/passing premise is absent in that declaration. The withdrawn C727_invalid__caller_assumed is not evidence, and neither compiler acceptance nor a missing-EXTERNAL complaint when EXTERNAL is present resolves the source issue.

requirements.oracle: C727_valid__unused_dummy_function admits an unused CHARACTER(*) dummy function. C727_valid__caller_assumed_repair retains its exact fixed-length CHARACTER(3),EXTERNAL source and execution ID as an independent compile admission control; its historical repair suffix no longer denotes an invalid/repair contrast. The disputed new C727_invalid__caller_assumed is withdrawn, with its interpretation facet restored to pending. Actual external definitions and invocations remain separate S7.4.4.2-006 effects with pending canonical linkage. Direct case IDs: C727_valid__caller_assumed_repair, C727_valid__unused_dummy_function.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No C727 negative is currently submitted. Success of the two source-valid admission controls does not decide the unused external-star declaration's legality. The p5 invocation/passing obligation cannot be applied when neither action occurs, and an externalness complaint cannot diagnose an already-EXTERNAL declaration. A future negative requires independent resolution of the exact source relation and a cause-specific contract. The retained C726 internal/module-result cases and their source bodies are unchanged.

requirements.title: Assumed-length functions exclude five function attributes
requirements.definition: A function name with an asterisk type-param-value cannot be an array, a pointer, elemental or pure, and cannot have the RECURSIVE attribute. The explicit RECURSIVE-attribute exclusion is distinct from 15.6.2.1 p3's rule against direct or indirect recursion for a subprogram defining an assumed-length function. The latter unnumbered execution restriction does not justify a runtime recursion trap test.
requirements.oracle: Five independent compile pairs retain ARRAY, POINTER, PURE, IMPURE ELEMENTAL or explicit RECURSIVE respectively while replacing only the assumed result length with 3. Array/pointer result declarations have a bounded header-to-declaration relation. The elemental case is explicitly IMPURE, the pointer target is live and length three, and no recursive call is introduced. Direct case IDs: C728_invalid__array, C728_invalid__elemental, C728_invalid__pointer, C728_invalid__pure, C728_invalid__recursive, C728_valid__array_repair, C728_valid__elemental_repair, C728_valid__pointer_repair, C728_valid__pure_repair, C728_valid__recursive_repair.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Generic function, character, array, pointer, pure or recursive nouns are not causal reports. Unsupported features, ASR/verifier failures and recovery at unrelated END statements cannot satisfy C728. Obsolescence warnings about assumed-length functions are not the intended prohibited-attribute diagnostic. ALLOCATABLE is not added to the source's exclusion list.
requirements.dependencies: C727 and 7.4.4.2 p5 (PDF 85); 8.1 p2 (PDF 117); 15.6.2.1 p3-p5 and 15.6.2.2 p3-p4 (PDF 353-354); 15.7/C1592/C1598/C15104-C15107 (PDF 359-360) and 15.9.1/C15118-C15121 (PDF 362) supply the separate pure/elemental control premises. B.3.6 (PDF 578) retains external assumed-length functions as obsolescent, not deleted; 4.2 p2(2)-(3) (PDF 46).

requirements.title: A legacy length-selector comma belongs only in a type declaration statement
requirements.definition: R722's optional comma is permitted only when the length-selector occurs in a declaration-type-spec in a type-declaration-stmt. A component definition, function prefix or ALLOCATE type-spec is not that statement context. The separate TYPE(intrinsic-type-spec) trailing-comma constraint C707 still applies; C729 alone does not override it.

pending.type-declaration-admission: Planned finite link to the future run R722_valid__comma, without a double colon. Preserve the existing C707_invalid__comma at tests/fixtures/declaration_type_specification_c707_comma/fixture.json under C707 rather than duplicating its TYPE-wrapper condition.

requirements.oracle: Three compile pairs delete only the optional length comma in component, function-prefix and ALLOCATE contexts. Their predicates require that comma/context cause and do not credit invalid-name or generic expected-token recovery. The allowed declaration-comma control remains a pending canonical link to R722. Direct case IDs: C729_invalid__allocate_comma, C729_invalid__component_comma, C729_invalid__function_comma, C729_valid__allocate_comma_repair, C729_valid__component_comma_repair, C729_valid__function_comma_repair.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The old CHARACTER* spelling remains legal without the comma in these other contexts, subject to their own rules. Do not confuse a declaration's attribute-list comma, an allocation-list separator or a function argument separator with R722's comma. Reporting is required capability, not mandatory fatal exit.

requirements.title: The legacy length-selector comma excludes a double-colon separator
requirements.definition: Even in an otherwise permitted type declaration statement, R722's optional comma is allowed only when the statement has no double-colon separator. The absence of this optional comma does not prohibit a double colon.

pending.without-double-colon: Planned finite link to R722_valid__comma. Also retain a no-comma, double-colon CHARACTER*3 :: item declaration in the repaired control, so this rule is not misread as a ban on all legacy declarations with ::.

requirements.oracle: One compile pair deletes only the character-length comma while retaining the double-colon separator. No attributes or initialization create another separator condition. The allowed no-double-colon comma path remains a pending R722 link. Direct case IDs: C730_invalid__double_colon, C730_valid__double_colon_repair.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No attributes or initialization are added, avoiding independent double-colon requirements or malformed attribute lists. C707 owns the distinct TYPE-wrapper exclusion.

requirements.title: Character statement-function and statement-dummy lengths are constant expressions
requirements.definition: Both a character statement function's length and the length of each character statement-function dummy argument are constant expressions. This is stronger than the ordinary specification-expression premise in a subprogram. It is not a restriction on every CHARACTER dummy or on automatic character variables. Statement functions remain obsolescent but conforming.
requirements.oracle: The function_length pair has only f of nonconstant length n while x has constant length 2; the dummy_length pair has only x of length n while f has constant length 2. Each repair changes only its nonconstant length to 2, with the same nonoptional INTENT(IN) integer n and otherwise valid specification-expression context. The declaration and adjacent statement-function definition form the diagnostic relation. Separate predicate sets retain the corresponding observed GNU function-f or argument-x cause and reject complaints about the other, already-constant subject at either allowed line. A separate run invokes the constant-length statement function and checks its exact result/length. Direct case IDs: C731_invalid__dummy_length, C731_invalid__function_length, C731_valid__constant_lengths, C731_valid__dummy_length_repair, C731_valid__function_length_repair.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A correct source point is not sufficient: the diagnostic must identify the actual nonconstant role, not the already-constant function or dummy in the opposite case. Cross-subject and ambiguous-subject alternatives are excluded without changing any Fortran input or minimal repair. No OPTIONAL or INTENT(OUT) n, array dummy, EXTERNAL statement-function name, uninitialized actual, transformational function reference or late statement-function definition is introduced. An obsolescence warning alone is not the required nonconstant-length report.

requirements.title: Omitting character kind selects the default character method
requirements.definition: CHARACTER without a supplied kind parameter denotes default character kind, whose value is KIND('A'). Supplying only length, including an individual length override, does not select a nondefault kind. Default character is not thereby equated with ASCII or ISO_10646.
requirements.oracle: Two unprofiled run programs check bare and length-only default CHARACTER, including legacy and individual lengths. Explicit default-character dummy calls test kind without assignment conversion; lengths and distinct values are checked separately. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_2_001_valid__bare, S7_4_4_2_001_valid__length_only.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No nondefault method or native ASCII mapping is required. Keyword spelling itself is already R704's CHARACTER alternative and is not given an invented misspelling rejection case.

requirements.title: Default character includes the required Fortran repertoire
requirements.source: 7.4.4.2 p3, first sentence; PDF 84, printed 70, lines 21-22.
requirements.definition: The default character method supports a set including the Fortran character set defined in 6.1: both letter cases, digits, underscore and the specified special characters. Additional repertoire is permitted but is not required by this inclusion obligation. Representing distinct required character values does not establish their graphics, font, source encoding or storage codes.
requirements.oracle: The run contains all 52 letter values, ten digits, underscore and the 32 explicitly enumerated Table 6.1 values. Exact segment/total counts and pairwise distinctness cover the 95 required values without ICHAR, native code distances, source-byte mapping or graphics credit. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_2_002_valid__repertoire.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A 95-member witness does not enumerate optional extra characters or certify how an external byte sequence becomes a source character. Source acceptance is not display-shape evidence. The existing Clause 6 catalogues and cases retain their primary ownership and limitations.

requirements.title: Every supported nondefault character set has a designated padding blank
requirements.source: 7.4.4.2 p3, last sentence; PDF 84, printed 70, lines 23-24.
requirements.definition: There is no general required repertoire for an arbitrary nondefault character set, but each such set has one character designated as its padding blank. Named ASCII/ISO 10646 set and collation definitions retain their own premises; a selected numeric kind value alone establishes neither source mapping nor the processor's designated padding value. The obligation is conditional on a nondefault method actually existing.

pending.named-nondefault-padding: Planned qualified run S7_4_4_2_003_valid__named_padding for one supported ASCII or ISO_10646 method proven distinct from default. First obtain independently documented designation of that method's blank and a proven in-range constructor. Assign a one-character value and then an empty value to fixed length-three objects; check the exact padding positions against that independent blank. Do not assume CHAR(32,k) or k_' ' is the designated padding value merely from a kind number.
pending.other-method-padding: Planned qualified run S7_4_4_2_003_valid__other_padding for one documented processor-named method outside the named-set witnesses. Apply the same one/zero-to-three length contrasts with same-kind values. If no such method/blank evidence exists, record the precise unavailable premise, not a passed or default-kind substitute.
pending.blank-designation-interface: Planned documentary record character-padding-blank: for each supported nondefault method, capture the versioned designation, its character identity and a legal constructor, separately from graphics and byte encoding. There is no portable inquiry that names the designated blank and no documentary case type in the current registry. Self-consistent assignment/comparison padding is not independent designation evidence.

requirements.oracle: Draft plan only. Finite nondefault padding cases require actual nondefault support and an independent blank oracle. Guard support before compiling declarations and retain runtime padding checks when a compiler lacks implementation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No arbitrary nondefault letter repertoire, byte width or cross-kind conversion is presumed. Default-only padding cases under S10.2.1.3-020 and conversion cases under S10.2.1.3-021 remain unchanged and cannot silently satisfy this nondefault-blank obligation. Documentary/interface gaps are genuine and remain pending.

requirements.title: Individual lengths override selectors and otherwise omitted length is one
requirements.definition: Character length can come from the CHARACTER selector or an individual *char-length in an entity or component declaration. The individual value overrides the selector's length for that entity/component only. Without an individual length, the selector's length applies; if neither specifies a length, it is one. The override does not change kind, other entities' lengths or array rank.
requirements.oracle: Four run programs separately check selector inheritance, individual entity overrides, individual component overrides and omitted length one. Overrides 2/0 leave siblings at length 5 and do not change kind. Initialized payloads and exact lengths are checked independently. Direct case IDs: S7_4_4_2_004_valid__component, S7_4_4_2_004_valid__default_one, S7_4_4_2_004_valid__entity, S7_4_4_2_004_valid__selector.
requirements.oracle_limitation: No default-integer LEN kind, storage size or inferred default character kind number is asserted. These are declaration-length effects, not new assignment-padding/truncation coverage. Existing canonical assignment cases remain separate.

requirements.title: A negative character length specification denotes zero length
requirements.source: 7.4.4.2 p5, first sentence; PDF 85, printed 71, lines 17-18.
requirements.definition: When a character length parameter specification evaluates to a negative value, the declared character entity has length zero. The specification's value may be negative while the resulting LEN parameter is nonnegative. Zero and negative expressions are not invalid twins, and a bare signed token must not be confused with a legal parenthesized negative expression.
requirements.oracle: Three valid run cases exercise constant, nonoptional-dummy-dependent and individual/component negative length specifications using small values -2, 0 and 3. They require resulting length zero rather than a diagnostic or trap; no empty position is accessed. requirements.title: Each assumed-length context has its own source of length
requirements.source: 7.4.4.2 p5, asterisk introduction and all five bullets; PDF 85, printed 71, lines 18-29.
requirements.definition:
An assumed-length character dummy takes its length from its effective argument; an assumed-length named constant takes it from its constant value. In the permitted ALLOCATE type-spec context, each object takes the length from its own effective argument. In a type guard, the associating entity takes it from the selector.

For an external assumed-length function result, every scope that invokes the function or passes it as an actual argument must declare a nonasterisk character length for the function name, or access such a definition by argument, host or use association. On invocation that parameter value supplies the result's length. The asterisk is not a return-time inference from the assigned text. The declaration whitelist, procedure characteristics, argument association and each function restriction still apply.
